definition: Pipelines, analytical products, and decision surfaces governed by schema, lineage, freshness, quality, and reproducibility.
counterexample: A content website with no analytical or data-processing contract.
nonGoals: Do not silently coerce malformed records.
Do not display metrics without source, timestamp, and definition.

requiredDecisions.question: Which source systems and schemas are authoritative?
Which freshness, completeness, and quality thresholds apply?
How are backfills, late data, retention, and recovery handled?
Which repository and branch policy are authoritative?
Who may approve promotion, merge, migration, deployment, and publication?
What rollback restores code, data, and external side effects?

requirements: Validate data at each declared boundary.
Record lineage, transformation version, and freshness metadata.
Make backfill and partial-failure behavior idempotent and observable.
verifications: Run representative, missing, duplicate, late, and malformed data fixtures.
Reproduce published metrics from versioned inputs.
Exercise partial failure, retry, and backfill.
authority: Resolution creates a candidate specification only; factory-ready, dispatch, merge, migration, deployment, publication, and courseware release require explicit human authority.
